A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedRDN research. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and matchable, including v2's supplementary Sections A–B. v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–3 report original classification, segmentation, cross-site generalization, ablation, and feature-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds FedBN comparisons, architecture experiments, expanded diagnostic analyses, and repeated-trial results in the supplement.

M1.justification: Both versions exchange client-level channel statistics, randomly select statistics for each training image and epoch, and use the client's own statistics at test time. Consolidated pseudocode and expanded explanations in v2 do not change this procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate classification on Office-Caltech-10 and DomainNet and segmentation on ProstateMRI, retaining the same domains/sites and Office-Caltech-10 cross-site evaluation. Added architecture and stability experiments remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: FedBN, previously only discussed, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 1–2, including its augmentation variants. This expands classification baselines from seven to eight and segmentation baselines from four to five; existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds an Office-Caltech-10 evaluation using ResNet-18 with other settings held fixed and extends the local-epoch sweep to DomainNet. Previously reported primary architectures, optimizers, training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged. Newly listed dataset split counts do not establish that existing splits changed.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds architecture robustness testing, extends epoch sensitivity from Office-Caltech-10 to DomainNet, and adds local-model feature visualizations alongside the retained global-model plots. Appendix B.1 additionally investigates random-seed stability, substantially broadening diagnostic validation.

E5.justification: v1 reports point results and curves without repeated-run uncertainty or significance tests. v2 explicitly reports two additional trials with different seeds, three-trial means and standard deviations, and paired t-test p-values for FedAvg augmentation comparisons across all three datasets in Tables 7–8.

E6.justification: v2 adds FedBN results, architecture results, expanded diagnostic findings, and three-trial summaries. New ResNet-18 accuracies include 43.74% for FedAvg and 56.70% with FedRDN in Table 5. All existing Table 1 values remain unchanged; Table 2 revises FedAvg's UCL Dice from 52.65 to 85.64 while retaining its reported average of 90.02.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 recasts v1's Gaussian sampling hypothesis as an approximate distribution model. v2 also explicitly writes the local empirical-risk formula in Equation 2. The feature-skew definition and normalization equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit claim to be the first input-level augmentation work for feature-distribution-skewed FL. The central contributions—plug-and-play FedRDN, mitigating feature shift, and improving existing FL methods—are retained.

C2.justification: The new limitation section explicitly states the visual-task focus and acknowledges the lack of theoretical analysis. v2 also explains FedBN's smaller gains, attributes ResNet-18's lower performance to dataset size, and expands the interpretation connecting local feature generalization to global feature alignment.

D1.justification: Table 6 newly provides per-client training, validation, and test counts. v2 specifies classification and segmentation losses and FedMix's lambda of 0.1. Existing baseline hyperparameters move to Appendix A.2; hardware and the promise of a future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds substantive discussion of FedPCL, FPL, and ADCOL, alongside additional supporting citations. The contrast with FedFA now emphasizes network modifications and resource costs. The overall positioning around input-level augmentation remains, while the explicit priority claim is dropped.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording and terminology, expands explanations, updates the author list, makes privacy a numbered subsection, renames diagnostic experiments, and moves baseline details into the supplement. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Two algorithms are consolidated; comparison tables are reorganized and highlight actual best scores; Figures 2–3 gain panels; and Tables 5–8 add architecture, dataset-split, and statistical displays. These substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: FedBN comparisons, architecture checks, and three-run statistics strengthen an already broad empirical study, while additional settings improve reproducibility and explicit limitations clarify evidential boundaries. The gains are limited by statistical checks covering only FedAvg augmentation variants and new reporting inconsistencies: Appendix A.1 states four DomainNet clients despite six in Table 6, and Table 8 labels segmentation results as Accuracy.
